steps.subject: Four Solar: 9 live Google ads, and the Meta Pixel on the landing page cannot fire
steps.body:
Hi,

I spend my week reading the public ad-transparency records for the Telangana solar market, and I put together a short report on what Four Solar is doing right now.

What it covers (pulled from Google's Ads Transparency Centre on 2026-11-10):

  - 9 live ads under your advertiser record, identity-verified as Four Solar Energy Systems Pvt. Ltd
  - two of them are Local ads with DIRECTIONS and CALL buttons, headed "Buy Solar Panels Online" and "Buy Solar Panels for Homes"
  - the ads point at foursolar.com, which I confirmed on the advertiser record

Nine live ads is real commitment, so I will be direct about what happens after the click.

Your homepage carries exactly one tracking tag, and it cannot fire. The Meta Pixel ID 1513606190140594 is in the page only as a <noscript> image fallback at source line 168 - I read the complete head, and there is no fbq() initialisation script anywhere in it. A visitor with JavaScript enabled, which is nearly all of them, is never counted. There is also no Google tag of any kind: no GA4, no GTM container, no Google Ads conversion tag. You are buying Search, Display, Local and YouTube clicks with nothing on the Google side measuring them.

Second, your own site contradicts itself on size. The stat tiles claim "250+ MW Solar Capacity Engineered & Executed" and "1,500+ sites"; the About section of the same page says "13+ years in solar EPC and 50 MW+ of projects delivered". Two capacity figures, five times apart, on one page.

Third, that broken <noscript> is also the single largest source of validation errors on the page: the checker reports 38 errors on the homepage - a duplicate <body>, stray end tags for head, div and header, and 24 of the 38 are style rules outside an @scope rule.

What is genuinely strong, and it is a lot: the enquiry form captures the monthly bill and the zipcode, there is a "Book a Site Visit" page and a WhatsApp click-to-chat, and your segment coverage - Industrial & MSME, Commercial & Institutional, Ground-Mounted MW-scale, PM-KUSUM, PM Surya Ghar, Gated Communities and Solar Kits - is broader than most of the installers I read. The proof exists. It is just not in front of the traffic you are paying for.

steps.body:
Hi,

I specialise in helping solar companies in Hyderabad get more installation enquiries, and I put together a full audit of what Green Carbon Hub is doing right now - your live ads on both platforms, and the page they land on.

What it covers (pulled from Google's Ads Transparency Centre and the Meta Ad Library on 2026-11-10):

  - 14 live Google ads under advertiser AR10321845347697033217, identity-verified as ECOILA PRIVATE LIMITED - not Green Carbon Hub
  - the copy buys "Get Subsidy Upto Rs 78000 - Solar Panels for Home" and "best solar rooftop service providers in Hyderabad" into greencarbonhub.com
  - 2 live Meta ads on your page - "Don't Just Install Solar. Keep It Performing!" (since Aug 30) and "Get Free Solar Checkup and Cleaning Today in Hyderabad!" (since Sep 10) - both clicking to fb.me

The entity mismatch is the first thing to fix: the spend is booked under a company name that does not match the brand on the ad, and a buyer who checks sees exactly that.

Second, the page the ads buy cannot carry the message. Your <title> is "GreenCarbonHub" - 14 characters, no service, no city, no offer - and your meta description element is shipped with an empty content attribute. Neither ad's headline appears anywhere in the page's own metadata.

Third, on measurement: you have GTM (GTM-TX4XRLT) and Meta Pixel (1088807282778475), which is more than most of the leads I write to. But a container is not a measurement - I could not read a GA4 measurement ID inside GTM-TX4XRLT - so 16 paid ads are running with no confirmed analytics behind them. And the one thing both Meta ads sell, lifetime maintenance, has no page of its own on the site.

Two smaller things that cost enquiries directly: the second phone number in your contact block dials the first one ("+91 9182445715" sits inside an <a href="tel:9182445300">), and there is no <h1> anywhere on the page - the checker reports an <h4> straight after an <h2>, a <button> inside an <a>, an unclosed <main> and a duplicate <body>, 34 errors in total, with most of your navigation commented out of the served HTML.

What is genuinely strong: the positioning is clear - a B2B2C net-zero marketplace with a four-step process - and the client strip names GE and the AP Food Processing Society. The offer is real. The page that has to carry it is not ready for the traffic you are already buying.
